findings.title: "Silence notifications" menu item does nothing in the list view
findings.body:
The list view now renders `RuleActionsButtons` with only `promRule` and no ruler rule. `AlertRuleMenu` still shows "Silence notifications", because `canSilence` is true via `useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities`. Clicking it calls `setShowSilenceDrawer(true)`.

However, the drawer only renders when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) && showSilenceDrawer`. Since `rule` is undefined here, `SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer` is never mounted and the click is a silent no-op.

The new GrafanaGroupLoader test checks that the silence item exists but never clicks it, so the bug is not caught. The drawer needs to work from the prom rule (e.g. by uid/labels), or the menu item should be hidden when no ruler rule is available.

findings.title: skipToken still reports Duplicate as supported, enabling Duplicate for data-source rules via Grafana permissions
findings.body:
With `skipToken`, `useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities` receives `undefined`. In that case `useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable` returns `loading: false`, so `MaybeSupported` becomes `AlwaysSupported`. Duplicate then resolves to `toAbility(true, AlertingRuleCreate)`, meaning `[true, true]` for any user with the global Grafana rule create permission.

`AlertRuleMenu` ORs this with the ruler result: `canDuplicate = rulerDuplicate || grafanaDuplicate`. For a data-source-managed rule (which always gets skipToken), Duplicate is therefore shown whenever the user can create Grafana rules. This holds even when the ruler is unavailable (e.g. vanilla Prometheus) or the user lacks external rule write permission. It affects the rule viewer, RulesTable and the v2 list.

When the rule is skipped, the hook should return `[false, false]` for every action.

findings.title: Delete and Pause actions silently disappear from the list view
findings.body:
Both menu items still require a ruler rule:
- Pause: `canPause && rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule) && ...` (line 123)
- Delete: `canDelete && rulerRule`

The list view (`GrafanaRuleListItem`) no longer passes a ruler rule. So even when the prom-based abilities say the user can pause or delete, these items are never rendered. Previously both actions were available from the list.

`canPause` also still feeds `showDivider`, so a divider can appear without a pause item. The new GrafanaGroupLoader test grants delete permissions yet asserts exactly 4 menu items, which locks this regression in.

Either support pause/delete from the prom rule (identifier + groupIdentifier are available) or document the removal explicitly.

findings.title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable
findings.body:
`useAllAlertRuleAbilities` used to compute `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`, which made Mimir federated groups (those with `source_tenants`) non-editable and non-deletable.

It now delegates to `useAllRulerRuleAbilities`, which hardcodes `const isFederated = false`. All existing consumers of `useAllAlertRuleAbilities`/`useAlertRuleAbility` (rule details, RulesTable, rule viewer) will now offer Update/Delete/Pause for federated rules. Editing those through the UI was previously blocked deliberately.

The federated check should be kept in the CombinedRule path, e.g. by passing the group or a flag.

findings.title: Prom-based abilities exclude Grafana recording rules from Export/Pause/Restore
findings.body:
The ruler version gates ModifyExport, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`, which is true for any Grafana-managed rule including recording rules.

The new prom version uses `isAlertingRule = prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` for all of these, despite the comment saying "All GrafanaPromRuleDTO rules are Grafana-managed by definition".

In the list view, which now relies only on these prom abilities, Grafana recording rules lose the Export menu item, and Pause/Restore are reported as unsupported. Only Silence should be restricted to alerting rules; the others should use `prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule)`.

findings.title: Missing React `key` on Grafana rule items in filtered list
findings.body:
The previous `<GrafanaRuleLoader key={key} .../>` was replaced with `<GrafanaRuleListItem .../>` without carrying over `key={key}`. The other branches (`DataSourceRuleLoader`, `UnknownRuleListItem`) still set it.

Grafana-origin items in this `rules.map` therefore have no key. React will emit "Each child in a list should have a unique key" warnings and fall back to index-based reconciliation, which can mis-associate per-item state (open menus, modals, silence drawer) as the list changes.

Add `key={key}` back.

findings.title: Rule view link lost the `returnTo` parameter
findings.body:
The removed implementation built the rule link as `createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`, { returnTo })` using `createReturnTo()`. The new component drops `returnTo`.

After opening a rule from the list (including a filtered search), the rule viewer's back navigation can no longer return the user to the same list/filter state. This is a UX regression unrelated to removing ruler requests.

findings.title: Stale doc comment says the group is loaded from the Ruler endpoint
findings.body:
The JSDoc still reads "Loads an evaluation group from Prometheus and Ruler endpoints", but this PR removed the ruler query. The component now only uses `useGetGrafanaGroupsQuery`.

The `expectedRulesCount` comment also still refers to the Ruler response. Similarly, `prometheusGroupsGenerator.ts` still says "preload ruler rules" and names the variable `cacheAndRulerPreload`, though no ruler prefetch happens anymore.
